name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
description: A 5th-century rock fortress built by King Kashyapa, rising 200 m above the surrounding plains. Climb past the Mirror Wall and the Lion Gate to the ruined palace gardens on the summit.
alt: Aerial view of Sigiriya Rock Fortress and its ruined palace rising above the misty jungle

name: Ella
description: A hill-country village known for hiking trails, tea estates and the Nine Arches Bridge. The slow blue train from Kandy is part of the experience.
alt: Collage of Ella: trains on the railway, tea plantations and hikers on the hills

name: Yala National Park
description: Sri Lanka's most visited national park and home to one of the world's densest leopard populations. Jeep safaris also reveal elephants, water buffalo, crocodiles, peacocks and many birds.
alt: Collage of Yala wildlife: a leopard, an elephant, water buffalo, a peacock and a crocodile

name: Galle Fort
description: A UNESCO World Heritage fortress on the south coast, first built by the Portuguese and expanded by the Dutch. Walk the ramparts past the lighthouse, old churches and boutique cafes.
alt: Galle Fort lighthouse, coastal ramparts and the sea

name: Arugam Bay
description: A laid-back east-coast surf town with one of the best right-hand point breaks in Asia, plus lagoons, fishing boats and golden sunrises.
alt: Arugam Bay beach, fishing boats, surfer and sunset lagoon

name: Jaffna
description: The cultural capital of the north, with the Nallur Kandaswamy Temple, the Dutch-era Jaffna Fort, a historic library and a distinct Tamil cuisine.
alt: Collage of Jaffna: the public library, Nallur temple, Jaffna Fort, clock tower and a gopuram

name: Matara
description: A southern coastal city near Dondra Head, Sri Lanka's southernmost point, with its tall lighthouse, palm-lined beaches and nearby whale and dolphin watching.
alt: Collage of Matara: palm beach at sunset, Dondra lighthouse, whale tail and dolphins

name: Nuwara Eliya
description: A cool hill town surrounded by tea estates, waterfalls and colonial-era buildings, nicknamed Little England. Gregory Lake and the railway through the plantations are favourites.
alt: Collage of Nuwara Eliya: tea plantations, a train, Gregory Lake and a waterfall

name: Kandy
description: The last royal capital of Sri Lanka, home to the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Kandy Lake and the spectacular Esala Perahera procession.
alt: Collage of Kandy: the Esala Perahera procession with decorated elephants, colonial hotel and Kandy Lake

name: Trincomalee
description: A natural deep-water harbour on the east coast with calm beaches, the hilltop Koneswaram Temple and whale watching in season.
alt: Collage of Trincomalee: a coastal headland, rocky cliffs, a whale, a Shiva statue and a beach with boats
